observation.visible_scene: A close-up of a wet, unlit clear glass bulb (Edison style) suspended from a black threaded socket and a vertical hanging wire, set against an out-of-focus green foliage background with soft bokeh circles. A diagonal cable covered in bead-like water droplets runs across the upper-right corner. Faint vertical rain streaks are visible against the background in many frames.
visible_changes: The hanging bulb sways very slightly, with small side-to-side / tilting oscillations of the bulb and its top wire relative to the frame edges, while its overall position stays roughly centered.
Transient rain streaks appear and disappear at different locations (e.g., left side, behind the bulb) from frame to frame, indicating falling rain passing through the scene.
The pattern of water droplets on the bulb's glass and on the diagonal cable shifts subtly as some droplets slide or merge.
The blurred green background and bokeh highlights drift and change brightness slightly, consistent with moving foliage and changing light during rain.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the rain began before this segment or continues after it.
Whether the bulb is ever powered on or lit.
The full extent of the bulb's swing outside these arbitrary crop boundaries.
uncertain_details: The framing stays largely fixed, so any camera motion is minimal/uncertain and cannot be separated confidently from the bulb's own sway.
The amplitude of the bulb's oscillation is small and may partly be a tilt rather than a translation.
Droplet movement on the glass is subtle and hard to distinguish from changes in focus and lighting.
